title: Plasma: the fourth state of matter
description: Ionisation turns a gas into a plasma, the matter of stars, lightning and the northern lights; a fusion plasma is hotter than the Sun's core but far thinner, and Lawson's triple product sets its target.

sources.title: Plasma (physics) (Wikipedia): Langmuir's name of 1928, quasi-neutrality, plasma as most of the visible ordinary matter
Sun (Wikipedia): core temperature 1.57 · 10⁷ K, core density up to 150 g/cm³
Solar core (Wikipedia): central pressure 26.5 million GPa, power density about 276.5 W/m³
Lightning (Wikipedia): channel temperature about 30 000 °C, average return-stroke current about 30 kA, plasma channel
Aurora (Wikipedia): heights (maximum near 100 km, few above 150 km), electrons of a few keV, oxygen 557.7 nm and 630.0 nm, nitrogen blue
Finnish Meteorological Institute: Northern lights (how often in Kilpisjärvi–Utsjoki, Sodankylä and Helsinki; the auroral oval about 2500 km from the poles)
ITER: Facts and figures (150 million °C, 830 m³, 500 MW from 50 MW, pulses of 400–600 s)
CIEMAT fusion wiki: ITER reference scenario (density about 1.0 · 10²⁰ m⁻³, R = 6.2 m, a = 2.0 m, 15 MA, 5.3 T)
Lawson criterion (Wikipedia): Lawson's classified 1955 Harwell report, published 1957; the triple product

Wurzel and Hsu, Progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criterion, AIP, doi 10.1063/5.0083990 (arXiv 2105.10954): ignition needs about 2.9 · 10²¹ keV·s/m³ near 14 keV
